subject: Insurance
title: 9/11 and Insurance
description: A quick win: understand 9/11 and Insurance.

hook.text: The September 11 attacks caused $40 billion in insured losses—the largest man-made insurance event in history.

buildup.text: Larry Silverstein had insured the World Trade Center just six weeks before the attacks.

discovery.text: Silverstein argued two planes meant two separate events—doubling the $3.5 billion payout. Courts partially agreed.

twist.text: After 9/11, terrorism insurance vanished from the market. The US government created TRIA to backstop terrorism risk.

climax.text: 9/11 proved that some risks are too large for private insurance alone. Government became the insurer of last resort.

punchline.text: $40 billion in claims. After 9/11, government had to backstop terrorism risk.

quiz.question: What did the US government create after 9/11 for insurance?
